reads.reason: a nameref's target is a name, not a value: the array it names decides how its subscripts are read
`${!x@K}`: the value of `x` is a name (`a[@]`), which picks the text of the transform; no value is said
`BASH_COMPAT` is read by bash itself, for the level of `<` in `[[ ]]`: no expansion copies it, and a value not known is `unknown`
the `TZ` that `date` gets in its environment for a worked example (exported, through the wrappers' slots): no expansion copies it
the `PATH` of the environment an example's `env` prints, on the made-up system: no expansion copies it
`$x` in arithmetic, pasted as text: `expansionValue` gives no value there (its word model reads no word in `$(( ))`); to move when it does
whether a variable is never empty (`DIR=/opt/app`), not its value: from the value or the static text of its word
whether the assignment word has static text where the value is not known (`B="$S/build"`): no source gives that fact yet
